done_when: The worker brief states the exact place and form of the Proof list (a commit message paragraph with one line per Done-when item, '<n>: <test>'), and forge handback writes a Proof list from the worker's report into a commit when the branch has none, so a native Claude round never fails the proof check for its form alone; new repos get it at init and existing repos on upgrade
why: Native Claude builders write their proof in the handback report instead of a Proof list paragraph in the last commit, so the Done-when proof check refuses close and items reach the round limit for that alone
